cards.body:
## Summary
Every per-school fact the AI and the plan layer need is spread over hand-written ternaries and three separate registries. Put each school's facts in one `SchoolKit` (rows, rules, brain, kind -> role / shape class / weight, resource reader, answer class, form-up check, dash-builds-resource flag, labels), keep one registry, and give the Fire and Air brains one shared skeleton (slot enumeration, build-rival branch, competence pick).

## Description
Today a plan change has to be written twice: archetypes.ts holds 7 `school === 'fire'|'air'` branches (roleOf, answersShape, weight, resourceOf, formUp, two Air-only dash branches). The kind -> class reading exists three times: fireShapeClass, airShapeClass, and roleOf's own kind switch. The build-rival branch and the level<2 random pick are copied verbatim between mage-ai-fire.ts and mage-ai-air.ts. The rules, brains and labels registries sit in three files. This is why every builds-census tuning step (the next item on the roadmap) touches four files per school, and why a third school (Earth is still on the plan) would mean editing about eight hand lists. A kit is data plus small functions: `kindOf(id)`, `shapeClass(kind)`, `role(spell)`, `weight(spell)`, `resource(a)`, `answers`, `answerUp(state, a)`, `movesForResource`, `label`, `named`, `slotCount(a)`, `offerable(...)`, `order(profile, target)`. archetypes.ts and the brains read the kit. School-specific priorities (Sunfall bank, Tempest/Form/Slipstream) stay in each brain as `priorities()` ahead of the shared pick. The kit registry resolves at call time, so the fire.ts load-order rule holds.

## Flow
- Commit 1: school-kit.ts builds kits from today's functions; school-kit.test.ts pins cases 1, 2 and 4 against the current behaviour.
- Commit 2: schools.ts dispatch, mage-ai-schools.ts brains and school-rivals.ts labels read `schoolKits`.
- Commit 3: archetypes.ts reads kit methods (no school literals); the brains use the shared skeleton; the source-scan case 3 and the pick-equality case 5 go green.
- Gate after each commit: the full `npm run gate`.

## Expected impact
The school literals in the plan and seam files go from 13 to 0. The build-rival branch and the competence pick each exist once. One kit file to add per school. Census-tuning changes to the plan layer land once, not per school. No outcome changes.

## Evaluation
Claim: the per-school knowledge becomes one derived kit and the simulation is unchanged.
Before: 0 of 6 acceptance cases pass (no school-kit module; 13 literals; the duplicate branches are present).
After: 6 of 6
Method: gate - vitest school-kit.test.ts + archetypes.test.ts + the replay goldens + CR parity vectors + census digests, all in npm run gate
Result: better
Gate: architecture

Registries: schools.ts:131 `const rules: Record<SlotSchool, SchoolRules> = { fire: fireRules, air: airRules };`, mage-ai-schools.ts:22 `const brains: Record<SlotSchool, SchoolBrain> = { fire: fireBrain, air: airBrain };`, school-rivals.ts:10-11 labels. cards.title: Plan-branch ledger: the builds census says WHY each build pressed or withheld
shared_surfaces: packages/core/src/arena/archetypes.ts (slot A's write set too: build after A, or tag the branches before A lands and let A carry them)
packages/core/scripts/builds-census.ts (operator report used by census:builds and week-census)
acceptance: case 1: fire_close rival at tier 2, player 2.5 m away (the archetypes.test.ts Ring fixture), trace enabled -> archetypeChoose returns the Ring slot and planTrace(state).get(rival.id) is { 'answer:pressed': 1 }
case 2: air_close rival at tier 2, Momentum 90, an aimed player projectile (the Air Form fixture) -> Air Form slot, branch 'answer:incoming'

case 3: fire_heavy rival at tier 1 with one seen threat and no payoff legal -> archetypeChoose returns undefined and the trace counts a withhold 'heavy:waiting' (a mana shortfall at tier 3 counts 'heavy:reserve')

case 4: a state without enablePlanTrace -> planTrace(state) is undefined; runBuildFight(seed, id) for 6 builds x 3 seeds -> the same stateHash with the trace on and off (the trace lives in a WeakMap, outside the hashed state)

case 5: summariseBuild(fights) -> a new `branches` share map over decisions summing to 1 (+-1e-9) and `withheldShare`; every existing summary field and the per-build digest equal to the pre-change run

case 6: pure whyLine({'light:bolt':0.5,'light:dash-out':0.3,'answer:incoming':0.2}) -> 'why light:bolt 50 light:dash-out 30 answer:incoming 20' (top 3, rounded %), printed after the roles segment of each report-builds line

cards.body:
## Summary
The owner tunes rival builds by running `census:builds`. It shows what each build cast, never why. Every archetype plan return gets a branch tag (answer:pressed, close:dash-in, light:alternate, heavy:waiting...). An opt-in per-state trace counts them. The census report prints the top branches and the share of decisions where the plan withheld.

## Description
D1 spent two rounds working out that Brand Drag is inert (Wrath is cast about 0.5 times per fight) and that Ring is cast almost only on the 'pressed' branch. builds-census.ts:51 still guesses the second fact by copying the plan's rule. archetypeChoose already knows the answer at each return and draws no random. plan-trace.ts holds `enablePlanTrace(state)`, `planTrace(state)` and `notePlan(state, actorId, branch)` over a WeakMap<ArenaState, Map<number, Record<Branch, number>>> (the rival-phases.ts pattern), so the hashed state never sees it. archetypeChoose notes its branch only when a trace is enabled. runBuildFight enables it, and summariseBuild adds `branches` and `withheldShare`. report-builds appends `why ...`. The Ring answer reading switches from the copied rule to the traced branch. Tagged JSON evidence carries the branches too.

## Flow
- Owner runs `npm --prefix packages/core run census:builds -- --only fire_heavy --count 40`.
- Each line now ends with, for example, `why heavy:waiting 41 heavy:bolt 33 heavy:payoff 12 | withheld 46%`. Wrath's starvation reads at a glance, with no probe to write.
- A plan edit followed by a re-run shows the branch mix move beside the win rate.

## Expected impact
The two D1 diagnoses that took probes (Wrath starvation, Ring pressed-only) become one census line. The duplicated pressed rule in the census goes away. Every later archetype tuning step shows its cause as well as its effect.

## Evaluation
Claim: the census reports the plan branch and the withhold share, with outcomes unchanged.
Before: 0 of 6 acceptance cases pass (no plan-trace module; PlanPick has no branch; the summary has no branches).
After: 6 of 6
Method: gate - vitest plan-trace.test.ts + builds-census.test.ts (hash equality trace on/off, digest equality) inside npm run gate
Result: better
Gate: direction
